messages:
cheng: ran a quick nsys on the regression run — timeline looks weird, memcpy H2D and a short host-side fence right before the KV prefetch kernel. attaching the small text excerpt below.

cheng: command i used: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt,nvtx -o out/trace_reg python -m bench.runner --workload=decode_p99`

cheng: timeline excerpt (nsys waterfall):
```
[CPU] thread0 sleep 2.4ms -> wake -> hostFence() -> cudaMemcpyAsync(H2D) 0.12ms -> kernel: kv_prefetch_async 3.8ms -> kernel: fused_attn_fp16 9.5ms
[CUDA] stream 2 memcpy H2D queued behind stream 0 kernel, visible gap on CPU 2.4ms
```

alicia: hmm that 2.4ms CPU sleep looks like preemption. do we have trace of which syscalls ran? could be GC or a background timer. :thinking_face:

cheng: i dumped perfetto CPU slices — it shows thread was preempted (SCHED_WAKE) by irq/softirq at the same time. not a Python GC.

ben: question: are the H2D memcpys using pinned buffers? if pageable, driver does staging that blocks and pins pages causing extra latency. try `cudaHostAlloc(..., cudaHostAllocPortable)` or our pinned pool.

dana: last week i reverted the pinned-pool fallback in the batched prefetcher because of an OOM issue, maybe this run hit pageable path again. could explain the memcpy->kernel serialization.

cheng: good call. i forced pinned allocs (local patch) and reran: p99 reduced ~8% and the host-side fence gaps vanished. reprofiled and timeline shows memcpy overlapped with a short prep kernel instead of waiting on CPU.

alicia: nice. do we know why pinned pool was disabled? if it was due to rarer OOMs we should add a soft-fallback and metrics rather than full disable.

ben: also worth checking stream priorities — if prefetch uses a low-prio stream we might see starvation when high-prio kernels occupy the copy engine. nvprof/nsight shows copy engine overlap but stream ordering still serialized.

cheng: i captured another run with nvtx ranges around the batcher. looks like when batch size bumps (seq len spike) the kernel selection picks a slower fused kernel and the batching heuristic triggers extra KV prefetches. combined effect = longer GPU kernels + more frequent host memcopies.

dana: action items:
- re-enable pinned pool with eviction guard and OOM metric (dana)
- add stream-priority test and force prefetch to high-prio for A/B (ben)
- add nvtx markers in batcher around kernel selection decision (cheng)
- add perf alert for hostside fence gaps (alicia)

perf-bot: perf regression alert: CI job "generator-e2e" shows +11.7% p99 since commit abc123 -> def456. linking trace: https://perf.internal/trace/3041598720

cheng: i'll attach the two nsys .qdrep slices to the ticket. will follow up after pinned pool patch and the stream-prio A/B run. thanks all. :thumbsup:
